summary: Serverless-first design: React Native (Expo), Supabase (BaaS), Supabase Postgres database. It matches the team's languages and is estimated at $34-$86 per month.

architecture.name: serverless
architecture.justification: Supabase runs the database, auth and APIs as a managed service, so there are no servers to size or patch and idle time costs little.

alternatives.why_not: Adds service boundaries, network calls and per-service deployment that this team does not need at this scale (team 2).
Steadier cost at sustained high load, but needs a host to size, patch and monitor.

frontend.justification: React Native (Expo) matches the team's javascript skills; has strong offline-first support on the client; open source; EAS free tier available.

alternatives.why_not: Kotlin + Jetpack Compose (Android native) scores 0.7 points lower overall, mainly on team skill fit (1.8 points) and compatibility with the rest of the stack (0.6 points).
Flutter scores 0.8 points lower overall, mainly on team skill fit (1.7 points).

tradeoffs: Heavier on 2 GB devices than Kotlin or Flutter
Native modules outside the Expo SDK need a custom development build

backend.justification: Supabase (BaaS) matches the team's javascript skills; is a managed backend, so there are no servers to run; generous free tier, predictable Pro plan.

alternatives.why_not: Firebase (BaaS) scores 1.8 points lower overall, mainly on vendor lock-in (3.6 points) and team skill fit (1.1 points).
Python + Django scores 2.3 points lower overall, mainly on team skill fit (1.9 points) and compatibility with the rest of the stack (1.2 points).

database.justification: Supabase Postgres can be placed in Mumbai (ap-south-1) to keep data in India; free tier then flat Pro pricing.

alternatives.why_not: Cloud Firestore scores 1.8 points lower overall, mainly on vendor lock-in (3.6 points) and team skill fit (1.1 points).

PostgreSQL (managed or self-hosted) scores 2.8 points lower overall, mainly on budget fit (2.3 points) and team skill fit (1.9 points). Estimated infrastructure about $75-$150/month versus about $32-$83/month.

tradeoffs: Paid plan needed for production SLAs

hosting.justification: The app is mobile-only and everything server-side runs on Supabase's managed platform in Mumbai (ap-south-1), so there is nothing to host separately; its plan and region are the hosting decision.

alternatives.why_not: Google Cloud Run scores 2.3 points lower overall, mainly on team skill fit (1.9 points) and compatibility with the rest of the stack (1.2 points).
DigitalOcean App Platform / Droplets scores 3.7 points lower overall, mainly on team skill fit (1.9 points) and time to market (1.4 points).

tradeoffs: Uptime, regions and resource limits follow Supabase's plan; moving off it later means re-hosting the backend.

supporting.justification: PostGIS (PostgreSQL extension): the description mentions GPS or location data, which needs spatial types and indexes; spatial types, GiST indexes and distance/within queries inside the existing PostgreSQL database; no extra service; already part of the chosen core stack.

alternatives.why_not: No other geo service satisfies the hard constraints.

tradeoffs: Spatial indexes add write cost on write-heavy tables; store points as geography in SRID 4326 from day one to avoid a migration

assumptions: Load estimate: peak about 20 requests/second and about 1.4M requests/month from 2K users in 12 months.
Usage-priced items are shown as a band (0.75x to 1.3x of the estimate) because load figures are order-of-magnitude.
Public list prices of each product, in USD, without taxes, committed-use discounts or developer time.
Observability (UptimeRobot / Better Stack uptime checks): about $0-$6/month

warnings.message: SMS to Indian numbers needs DLT registration (entity, sender ID and message templates) with a telecom operator before launch; allow one to two weeks.
DPDP Act: record consent, support erasure and correction, notify breaches, and take extra care with children's data. Cross-border transfer is allowed except to countries the government restricts.

CERT-In directions (April 2022) apply to services used in India: enable logs on all systems, keep them for 180 days within India, sync clocks to an NTP source and report cyber incidents within 6 hours. Size log retention and storage for this.
The description mentions low-end phones: keep the app bundle and screen count small, avoid heavy web views and animations, and test release builds on a 2 GB RAM device.

The description mentions weak or intermittent networks: save every write locally first and sync in the background with retries, use client-generated ids so a retried upload is not stored twice, and keep payloads small. Resize and compress photos on the device (about 1280 px on the long edge) and upload them in resumable chunks.
Offline edits made on several devices will collide when they sync; decide the rule per record type (server wins, last write wins per field, or keep both for review) before building the sync layer.
GPS or location data is personal data under DPDP: record consent with each point, keep only the precision you need, and set a retention period.

Some Indian ISPs blocked Supabase's shared *.supabase.co domain in late February 2026 until it was restored on 3 March 2026. Serve the API from your own custom domain so a block on the shared domain does not take the app offline (supabase.com/blog/navigating-regional-network-blocks).

assumptions: No extra inputs supplied; neutral defaults are used (learning appetite medium, lock-in tolerance medium, budget strictness firm, no hiring plan, no mobile preference).
Description mentions low-end devices; client footprint is weighted higher.
Description mentions poor connectivity; sync and payload size are weighted higher.
No cache layer: about 20 requests/second and 2,000 users in 12 months are served directly by the database or BaaS.
No queue: background work is light enough for the backend or the provider's own webhooks and functions.
